chunks: Three - Ali ibn Ahmad narrated to us, from Ubaydillah ibn Musa al-Abbasi, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'O Muhammad! Whoever narrates to you from us regarding timing, do not hesitate to consider him a liar, for we do not assign a specific time to anyone.'

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah, referring to Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)
key_terms.تَوْتِيْتًا: Timing or assigning a specific time

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about those who narrate specific timings for the Imam's appearance?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Kitab al-Ghayba*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the principle of 'no specific timing' (la nuwaqqit) for the reappearance of the Qa'im, distinguishing between the Imams' absolute knowledge of the hour and their deliberate concealment of it from the general public. This serves as a foundational Shia doctrine against the 'speculators' (al-muwaqqitun) who claimed precise dates, emphasizing that while the time is known to God and the Imams, it remains hidden from the masses to preserve the mystery of the Occultation.
